designDecisionsAndRationale: A small CodeRenderer interface (renderer-types.ts) that CanvasRenderer satisfies structurally, so canvas code stays untouched (DR-1).
TextLayout remains the sole geometry authority; the DOM renderer never measures text or reads layout, so both backends share caret/selection geometry (DR-3).
Virtualized window with keyed line elements (WeakMap keyed by ShapedRun[] identity) and transform-only scroll (DR-4, DR-5).
Playing highlights as tracked class toggles with an LRU-bounded key map (DR-6).
compare.mjs reuses runMeasurement, the silent sink and unchanged thresholds; pure helpers in compare-stats.mjs are unit-tested because the sandbox cannot bind localhost (DR-10).
setPhases sets layout.phases so shaping time is attributed identically in both modes (core Key Point 17).
intentionalTradeoffs: The 1,000-line document is a slice of the 20,000-line fixture (sliceWorkload) because the fixture asserts 1 MiB.
Raw sample files are downsampled (stride 32, auto-doubled to fit 870,000 bytes per run).
Gate failures of either renderer are reported results, not blockers; no rerun-until-pass.
Canvas behavior failures unrelated to the seam are recorded for the wf/canvas owner, not fixed here.
supportedEdgeCases: Japanese IME preedit and composition bars; emoji and non-ASCII caret alignment within 2 px.
Long lines rendered by horizontally culled 256-cluster chunks.
DPR change and resize without line rebuilds.
Markup-like document text rendered literally (textContent only).
Highlight and overlay caps with dropped counters; dispose leaves no nodes.
outOfScopeEdgeCases: WebKit JS heap growth (reported as unavailable).
Real (non-synthetic) WebKit touch, IME and clipboard.
